corrections.text: The article states, citing Al Jazeera, that "CCIA and SEAT had countered that the law would treat 'virtually the entire internet' as 'commercial speech the government could more readily ban.'" This quote does not appear in the cited Al Jazeera report. The verbatim language appears only in SCOTUSblog's coverage, which attributes it solely to the students' group (SEAT) in its emergency filing -- not jointly to CCIA. CCIA's own SCOTUSblog-reported argument concerned the Fifth Circuit's ruling "upset[ting] the status quo" and imposing "enormous and unrecoverable compliance costs," not the "entire internet"/"commercial speech" language.
